content.text:
Short answer up front
I can’t “prove” a subjective claim like “disregards human rights.” But the public record shows a consistent pattern of actions and positions by House Speaker Mike Johnson that major civil‑liberties and human‑rights groups argue would curtail core rights (bodily autonomy, equality, privacy, asylum, and democratic participation). Here are the best‑documented examples, with primary sources.

Key evidence from the public record
- Democracy and voting rights
  - Led House Republicans’ amicus brief supporting Texas v. Pennsylvania, the Trump‑backed lawsuit asking the Supreme Court to throw out certified 2020 presidential results in four states; the Court rejected the case for lack of standing. Johnson also voted to object to certifying electoral votes on Jan. 6, 2021. These actions were widely criticized as attempts to overturn millions of lawfully cast votes. ([scotusblog.com](https://www.scotusblog.com/2020/12/justices-throw-out-texas-lawsuit-that-sought-to-block-election-outcome/?utm_source=openai))
- Reproductive rights
  - Original cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act (118th Congress H.R. 431), which declares constitutional rights begin “at the moment of fertilization,” a personhood policy that would effectively ban abortion nationwide (and could have broader implications). The official cosponsor list shows “Rep. Johnson, Mike [R‑LA‑4]” as an original cosponsor. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/431/cosponsors))
  - In a 2005 op‑ed, Johnson likened abortion to “a holocaust,” reflecting a maximalist position on restricting abortion access. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/house-speaker-mike-johnson-abortion-holocaust/?utm_source=openai))
- LGBTQ equality
  - In multiple Shreveport Times columns in 2003–2005, Johnson called homosexuality “inherently unnatural,” a “dangerous lifestyle,” opposed decriminalizing gay sex (Lawrence v. Texas), and warned same‑sex marriage would imperil democracy. These writings were documented by CNN and summarized by the Washington Post. He later voted against the federal Respect for Marriage Act in 2022 (House roll call shows “Johnson (LA) — Nay”). ([amp.cnn.com](https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2023/10/25/politics/mike-johnson-gay-sex-criminalization-kfile?utm_source=openai))
- Privacy and surveillance
  - As Speaker, Johnson advanced H.R. 7888 (Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act) reauthorizing FISA Section 702 for two years without adding a blanket warrant requirement to search Americans’ communications; a bipartisan amendment to require warrants failed 212–212. Civil‑liberties groups warned the package maintains or expands warrantless surveillance. ([democraticwhip.house.gov](https://democraticwhip.house.gov/floor-resources/amendment-tracker/hr-7888-reforming-intelligence-and-securing-america-act?utm_source=openai))
- Asylum and immigrant rights
  - Supported and voted for H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act (House passage 219–213, nearly all GOP yeas). Leading refugee and human‑rights organizations say H.R. 2 would “gut the U.S. asylum system,” restart “Remain in Mexico,” and violate international protection norms. ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2023209))

Why this matters
- The items above are not stray statements; they are official votes, bills he cosponsored, litigation positions he led, and a surveillance package he moved as Speaker. Major rights organizations (HRW, ACLU, AAJC, HIAS) argue these actions—taken together—would reduce legal protections for voting, reproductive autonomy, LGBTQ families, privacy against warrantless searches, and the right to seek asylum. Reasonable people can differ on policy, but the documented record supports the claim that his agenda would narrow these human and civil rights. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/breaking-news/2023/04/18/us-house-border-bill-would-gut-us-asylum-system-border-proposal-would?utm_source=openai))

2) Sources I considered trustworthy (and why)
- Congress.gov (Library of Congress)
  - Reasoning 1: Official, primary legislative database (bill texts, histories, cosponsors, amendments). ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/431/text?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used to verify Johnson’s original cosponsorship of the Life at Conception Act (H.R. 431) and details of the failed warrant‑requirement amendment to H.R. 7888. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/431/cosponsors))
- Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives
  - Reasoning 1: Official roll‑call vote records. ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021260?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used to confirm Johnson’s “Nay” on the Respect for Marriage Act (Dec. 8, 2022) and House passage of H.R. 2 (May 11, 2023). ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2022514))
- Associated Press
  - Reasoning 1: Nonpartisan wire service with rigorous editorial standards. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/8cd7c5a9e6ae69635bbb4624cc78e5c5?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used for Johnson’s leading role in post‑2020 efforts and concerns that raised for democratic succession. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/8cd7c5a9e6ae69635bbb4624cc78e5c5?utm_source=openai))
- SCOTUSblog
  - Reasoning 1: Highly regarded legal reporting focused on the Supreme Court. ([scotusblog.com](https://www.scotusblog.com/2020/12/justices-throw-out-texas-lawsuit-that-sought-to-block-election-outcome/?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used for precise description and outcome of Texas v. Pennsylvania. ([scotusblog.com](https://www.scotusblog.com/2020/12/justices-throw-out-texas-lawsuit-that-sought-to-block-election-outcome/?utm_source=openai))
- CNN (KFILE reporting)
  - Reasoning 1: Mainstream outlet; the KFILE unit published primary-source‑based reporting on past op‑eds. ([amp.cnn.com](https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2023/10/25/politics/mike-johnson-gay-sex-criminalization-kfile?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used to source verbatim language Johnson used about LGBTQ people and his stance on decriminalization. ([amp.cnn.com](https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2023/10/25/politics/mike-johnson-gay-sex-criminalization-kfile?utm_source=openai))
- Washington Post
  - Reasoning 1: National paper of record with strong standards and documentation. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2023/10/26/mike-johnson-house-speaker-lgbtq-religion/?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used to contextualize Johnson’s long‑standing culture‑war advocacy and quote his earlier descriptions of same‑sex relationships. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2023/10/26/mike-johnson-house-speaker-lgbtq-religion/?utm_source=openai))
- CBS News
  - Reasoning 1: Mainstream national news with editorial oversight. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/house-speaker-mike-johnson-abortion-holocaust/?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used for Johnson’s 2005 op‑ed calling abortion “a holocaust.” ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/house-speaker-mike-johnson-abortion-holocaust/?utm_source=openai))
- ACLU
  - Reasoning 1: Long‑standing civil‑liberties organization; credible on surveillance/civil‑liberties law (discloses its advocacy posture). ([aclu.org](https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/aclu-urges-congress-to-vote-no-on-section-702-reauthorization-if-widely-supported-civil-liberties-protections-arent-included?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used to assess rights implications of Section 702 reauthorization without warrants. ([aclu.org](https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/aclu-urges-congress-to-vote-no-on-section-702-reauthorization-if-widely-supported-civil-liberties-protections-arent-included?utm_source=openai))
- Human Rights Watch
  - Reasoning 1: Major international human‑rights NGO with transparent methodologies; advocacy oriented but widely cited. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/breaking-news/2023/04/18/us-house-border-bill-would-gut-us-asylum-system-border-proposal-would?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used for analysis that H.R. 2 would “gut” asylum protections and harm families/children. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/breaking-news/2023/04/18/us-house-border-bill-would-gut-us-asylum-system-border-proposal-would?utm_source=openai))
- Asian Americans Advancing Justice | AAJC
  - Reasoning 1: Established civil‑rights group focused on privacy/surveillance impacts on communities. ([advancingjustice-aajc.org](https://www.advancingjustice-aajc.org/press-release/advancing-justice-aajc-denounces-reauthorization-section-702-fisa-and-passage?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used for expert critique that RISAA/702 “significantly expands” warrantless surveillance and threatens civil liberties. ([advancingjustice-aajc.org](https://www.advancingjustice-aajc.org/press-release/advancing-justice-aajc-denounces-reauthorization-section-702-fisa-and-passage?utm_source=openai))
- HIAS (Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society)
  - Reasoning 1: Historic refugee‑protection NGO; credible expertise on asylum systems. ([hias.org](https://hias.org/statements/hias-opposes-secure-border-act-2023/?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used for assessment that H.R. 2 would “essentially end the U.S. asylum system.” ([hias.org](https://hias.org/statements/hias-opposes-secure-border-act-2023/?utm_source=openai))
- Democratic Whip and Republican Cloakroom sites
  - Reasoning 1: Official House leadership pages that publish vote summaries; partisan, but vote tallies are factual and match Clerk data. ([democraticwhip.house.gov](https://democraticwhip.house.gov/floor-resources/amendment-tracker/hr-7888-reforming-intelligence-and-securing-america-act?utm_source=openai))
  - Reasoning 2: Used to corroborate outcomes and key amendment results on H.R. 7888 and H.R. 2. ([democraticwhip.house.gov](https://democraticwhip.house.gov/floor-resources/amendment-tracker/hr-7888-reforming-intelligence-and-securing-america-act?utm_source=openai))

3) Sources I considered not trustworthy (or not suitable for evidence here)
- None relied upon for claims above.
  - I purposely avoided using partisan blogs or unsourced social posts. Where advocacy organizations were cited (ACLU, HRW, AAJC, HIAS), I paired them with primary government records (Congress.gov, Clerk) and reported facts from mainstream outlets to ground the analysis in verifiable evidence. For misattributed quotes circulating online, I cross‑checked with fact‑checkers rather than rely on viral posts. ([snopes.com](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/johnson-studies-homosexual-relationships/?utm_source=openai))

If you want, I can extract and attach the specific House roll‑call lines for any of the votes above, or dig into additional areas (e.g., specific bills he backed on transgender health care or additional privacy votes).
